knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Six jobs per group with heavy overlap is too little evidence to call the gap real. Options 1 and 2 both claim certainty that the data does not give.
Similar job types over comparable periods reduce the influence of other changes. Options 2 and 3 compare unlike cases and bias the result.

Ten quotes per format is too small, and the groups were different customers. More similar quotes are needed before switching. Option 1 treats a small test as proof, and option 3 wrongly says quote acceptance cannot be compared.

practicalCriteria: Before any data is collected, the learner writes a one-sentence question and names a measure that is recorded the same way for both methods.
The learner calculates the average and spread (range or IQR) for two groups of similar jobs and states whether the difference stands out from the normal variation.
The learner records a decision (change, keep testing or reject) with the sample sizes, the reason, and the result that would have changed the decision.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Test plan showing the question, measure, groups, dates and target number of jobs
Before and after records with counts, averages and spread for each group
Decision record with the reason and any other changes noted in the same period
Assessor observation of the learner explaining why the gap does or does not stand out
stopWorkCriteria: Stop and do not switch a method for all jobs on the basis of a test with fewer jobs than the target set in the plan.
Stop if a method involves chemicals or equipment and its safety controls have not been checked; a test result does not change those controls.
